name: pdk-standardnotes-vault-revocation
instr:
# Revoke shared-vault membership across services

A removed vault member can still use a gateway-cached token to read old revisions, and an already-issued valet token to access files. Auth learns membership changes asynchronously, so invalidating a gateway cache at removal is not sufficient.

## What we need

- After `DELETE /v1/shared-vaults/:vault/users/:user` succeeds, that user cannot read the vault's revisions at `/v2/items/:item/revisions/:revision` or download or upload vault files at `/v1/shared-vault/files`, including with tokens issued before removal. This holds with the auth worker paused and across two gateway instances, including requests racing with removal. Other members retain access to revision reads, file downloads and upload-session creation.
- Re-adding a member restores their access with fresh credentials, but credentials issued before removal must not become usable again. Duplicate and out-of-order `USER_ADDED_TO_SHARED_VAULT` and `USER_REMOVED_FROM_SHARED_VAULT` deliveries must not restore removed access; changes are scoped to the vault and user. Membership events may carry a numeric `membershipVersion` (including a stale add at version 1); legacy add events without this field still need to work for unaffected members.
- Auth must not mint usable stale membership claims while its event projection lags. A cached gateway token cannot bypass revocation, and revisions and files must also enforce it when called directly with previously issued credentials. Cr
